newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee dips as banks seek to go long on dlr.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee dips as banks seek to go long on dlr.

text.p: The Indian rupee slipped to 35.87/88 against the dollar in late morning deals on Tuesday as banks sought to go long on dollars apprehending a weakening of the rupee, dealers said.

The dollar opened the day at 35.86/87 rupees against the previous close of 35.85/86 in what dealers described as a reaction to aggressive dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Monday.
"They (the RBI) bought (dollars) upto 35.86 level yesterday," said a bank dealer. "It was a clear signal they wanted a correction in the exchange rate."
"With major European nations welcoming recent dollar gains, it is perplexing to see the rupee holding out," said a European bank in its forex commentary.
The spot rupee was quoted at 35.865/875 in latest deals.
Premia on the forward dollar reacted to low overnight call rates, dealers said.
July dollars opened at 1.25/1.26 rupees and was quoted at 1.27/1.30 rupees in the latest deals, dealers said.
